description.summary: the window list, with placement and process, and control over it

protocol.description:
An AI agent that works on the desktop needs to know what windows exist, where they are, which process owns them and which one has focus, and to bring one forward, move it to another workspace or monitor, or put it out of the user's way. This protocol gives all of that to one trusted client, the agent daemon, which speaks to agents on the compositor's behalf.
Each window object names the same window as an ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 through its identifier, so the two lists can be joined. Workspaces are named by the id their ext_workspace_handle_v1 announces.
Only the agent daemon can bind the manager global: a compositor exposes it to clients it has verified, not to every privileged client.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_window_control_manager_v1

description.summary: the list of windows and the focus

interface.description: On bind the compositor sends a window event for every mapped toplevel, each followed by that window's description ending in done, then focus, then done on the manager. Afterwards windows that map get a window event, and changes arrive as further events on their objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Window objects created from it stay valid until destroyed individually, but receive no further events.

request.name: get_agent_workspace
request.description: Asks for the identifier of the agent workspace, the workspace windows launched with WORKSPACE=headless map to; agent_workspace answers. The compositor creates it on demand.

event.name: window
event.description: A window exists. Its description follows on the new object and ends with done.

event.name: focus
event.description: The window with the user's keyboard focus, or null when no window has it. Sent on bind and on every change.

event.name: agent_workspace
event.description: The ext_workspace identifier of the agent workspace, in answer to get_agent_workspace. Empty when the compositor has none.

interface.name: crownos_window_v1
interface.description: A toplevel as the agent daemon sees it. Events are grouped: a run of property events is followed by done, after which the object is consistent. closed is the last event; the client should then destroy the object, and requests on it are ignored.

entry.name: agent_workspace
entry.summary: on the agent workspace, out of the user's sight

request.name: focus
request.description: Gives the window keyboard focus, restoring it if minimized and switching the user to its workspace. A window on the agent workspace is shown there, not moved.

request.name: close
request.description: Sends the client an xdg_toplevel.close. The window may refuse.

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move the window to a workspace

request.description: Moves the window to the workspace with this ext_workspace identifier. An unknown workspace is ignored.

request.name: make_visible

description.summary: bring an agent's window onto the user's screen

request.description: Moves a window from the agent workspace to the user's focused workspace and focuses it. Does nothing to a window already there.

request.name: make_hidden

description.summary: send the window to the agent workspace

request.description: Moves the window to the agent workspace, creating it if needed, so it keeps running out of the user's sight.

request.name: set_rectangle
request.description: Sets the position and size of a floating window in its output's logical coordinates. Ignored for tiled windows.

event.name: identifier
event.description: The identifier the window's ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 carries. Sent once, first.

event.name: process
event.description: The pid of the client that owns the window's surface, as the kernel reported it when the client connected. 0 when unknown, as for a window of a remote X11 client.

event.name: placement
event.description: The window's content rectangle in its output's logical coordinates, the output's name and the ext_workspace identifier of its workspace.

request.name: move_to_output

description.summary: move the window to an output

request.description: Moves the window to the output with this name, as the placement event names it, onto that output's active workspace. When the compositor switches workspaces on all outputs together, the window goes to the workspace at the index of its current workspace instead. An unknown output, and an output that is not part of the desktop, such as a hidden virtual output, is ignored.
